hook_text: Snap a twig off a spekboom, push it into the soil, and wait. A whole new plant appears.
clip_script: Graaff-Reinet school garden. Mrs Booysen snaps off a spekboom twig, pushes it into damp soil, and waits. A few weeks later? Roots! A brand new plant, for free. Now a bean seed on wet paper. It swells. The coat splits. A root goes down. A shoot goes up. Test time: wet and warm? It grows. Wet but in the fridge? Nothing. Dry but warm? Nothing. Seeds need water and warmth. And the light? Not yet. Only once the leaves come up.
visual_style: Whiteboard spekboom cutting growing white roots in a jar, then a bean seed splitting open with a root going down and a shoot going up.
mood: Gentle and amazed, like watching a garden wake up.
pacing: Cutting first, then a seed opening step by step, then the warm and cold test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and grow a new plant from a cutting at home.
